provenance.prompt:
One isolated male Holden voice, a dry conversational historical storyteller. Begin directly with "The U.S. Army". No introduction, no instructions spoken, no other voices, music or effects. Speak every word between NARRATION START and NARRATION END exactly once, with clear connected phrasing and a curious, restrained tone. End immediately after "move".
NARRATION START
The U.S. Army fooled German forces with inflatable tanks and fake battle sounds. In nineteen forty-four, a secret American unit arrives in Europe with a strange job: make the enemy see an army that isn't there. Its official name is the Twenty-third Headquarters Special Troops. Today, we call it the Ghost Army. These are real soldiers, including artists, engineers, radio operators, and sound technicians. But some of their heavy equipment can be folded up. Crews unpack rubber decoys, spread them across the ground, and pump them into the shapes of tanks and other military vehicles. From nearby, the trick looks almost ridiculous. A few men can pick up a tank. From an enemy reconnaissance aircraft, the same shape can look like armor waiting to move.
NARRATION END
